parts.text: Which claim correctly states what regrouping or reordering does to the product?

options.text: $(-4) \times \bigl((-3) \times 5\bigr)$ and $\bigl((-4) \times (-3)\bigr) \times 5$ both equal $60$, and any order of these factors keeps that product.
Call the answer the product alone, with no check that the factors stay these same integers.
Treat the product as unchanged even when the factors are no longer these integers.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Integer multiplication is associative and commutative, so regrouping or reordering these factors keeps the product $60$.

teacher.key_rationale: Associativity and commutativity keep the product $60$ under regrouping or reordering. Naming "product" alone, or changing the factors, misses that hinge.
